# episko

> A free, open-source desktop app for macOS on Apple silicon and Windows 10/11 that runs Claude Code, Codex and 20 other coding agent CLIs at once, each in its own real terminal. Claude Code and Codex report live status, model, context use, cost, running tool and permission requests into one view, with history and resume. The others run as plain terminals with no status reporting.

episko is built by Respeak GmbH (Karlsruhe, Germany) and released under the MIT licence. It is an independent project, **not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Anthropic, OpenAI or the other agent providers**. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic, PBC.

The name comes from Greek ἐπίσκοπος (*episkopos*), "the one who watches over".

## What it does

- **Runs sessions in parallel.** Each session is a separate process in its own PTY, and these are the agents' real interactive terminals, so you can type into them. Claude Code and Codex are integrated; OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Amp, Qwen, Kimi and others run as plain terminals. On macOS a Claude Code session can also run in an external Ghostty, Terminal.app or iTerm2 window.
- **Shows what Claude Code and Codex are doing.** Per session: phase (idle, thinking, working, done, needs-you, error), model, context-window use, dollar cost, elapsed time, the tool currently running, and a short history of recent tool calls with latencies.
- **Answers permission prompts.** When Claude Code or Codex asks to run a command, episko shows the request with a risk label and lets you allow it, deny it, or jump into the terminal, so you don't have to hunt for the blocked window.
- **Tracks usage limits.** Reads your 5-hour and weekly Claude limits and Codex's rate-limit windows and forecasts your pace, warning from amber to red before you hit a wall. Includes a usage dashboard: daily spend heatmap, tokens by model, token composition, and cost attributed per project.
- **Launches into git worktrees.** The new-session dialog lists the repo, its worktrees and branches, and can create a new worktree for a session so parallel agents don't collide in one checkout.
- **Gives every project a dashboard.** Clicking a project opens its week: commits and sessions summarised a day at a time, open GitHub issues and pull requests, the repo's checkouts, and shared notes. An agent can be dispatched straight at an issue: episko creates a worktree, sends the prompt, and writes a claim to the issue so a colleague's agent doesn't start the same work twice. A generated per-day work log about the project (never about your spend) can be committed as `.episko/digest.md` so the team reads one shared history.
- **Shows each project's commit graph.** Lanes, merges, branch and tag labels, read one page at a time and fetched as you scroll, so a huge repo opens as fast as a small one.
- **Organises the sidebar your way.** Projects can be grouped under named headings and folded away; a folded group still shows the most urgent status glyph it hides. Task chains (`dependsOn`) fold into a single row carrying the worst step's status, and open into a tiled stage.
- **Keeps a whole-machine history.** Every Claude Code and Codex session on the machine, episko's or not, is read from the agent's own records: searchable, scoped by project and day, reopenable.
- **Finds sessions started elsewhere.** Claude Code sessions launched outside episko are discovered and listed read-only, with jump-to-terminal on macOS (the exact tab) and Windows (the hosting window).
- **Survives restarts.** Claude Code and Codex sessions are resumed through the agent's own history, so conversation state belongs to the agent and episko doesn't have to capture it. Even a webview reload rebuilds every pane and re-adopts the running processes, scrollback included.
- **Runs your project's own tasks.** The task definitions a project already ships (`.episko/tasks.toml`, `.vscode/tasks.json`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `package.json` scripts, a `justfile`, `Taskfile.yml`, `mise.toml`, a `Makefile`, `Cargo.toml`) run in the same panes as the agents, started from a **▶ Run** picker (⌘⇧R) or the command palette. A task run *is* a session: its exit code becomes its status (0 = done, non-zero = error), so it shows up in the sidebar, the attention badge and the tray like anything else. Runs are deliberately un-instrumented (no telemetry, no cost) and go through a login shell so they inherit your PATH and version-manager shims. Task discovery never executes the project: tools whose listing would evaluate the repo sit behind a trust gate, and tasks that can't run (needing an editor, or an attach-type debug config) are listed with the reason rather than hidden.
- **⌘K command palette** to jump between sessions or launch a project, and a **settings window** (⌘,).

## How it works

For Claude Code, episko generates a throwaway `--settings` file per launch, containing a `statusLine` command and lifecycle hooks that POST to a localhost HTTP server inside the app. This means no global `~/.claude` mutation and no transcript-file scraping: instrumentation is per-launch and disappears with the temporary file. For Codex, episko starts a loopback App Server and attaches the real TUI to it with `--remote`. Any other CLI reports no status, because episko never guesses state from screen text.

Your agents talk to their own APIs with your own login. episko listens on 127.0.0.1, has no server of its own and sends nothing to Respeak.

Built with Tauri v2: a Rust backend with a vanilla-TypeScript frontend.

## Requirements

- At least one supported agent CLI on your PATH (Claude Code, Codex or one of the terminal-only CLIs), with your own access to it.
- macOS on Apple silicon, or Windows 10/11. Linux is not yet packaged.
- On Windows the embedded terminal is supported; the external-terminal engines (Ghostty, Terminal.app, iTerm2) are macOS-only.
